Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let  
\[
D=\{1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250\}
\]
be the set of positive divisors of \(250\), and write
\[
M_d=\max A_d\qquad(d\in D).
\]
We will prove that
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250} M_d\ge 499
\]
and then construct an example attaining \(499\).

---

## 1. Atomic decomposition of the sets

From the condition with \(i=j\),
\[
|A_i|=\gcd(i,i)=i.
\]
If \(i\mid j\), then
\[
|A_i\cap A_j|=\gcd(i,j)=i=|A_i|,
\]
so
\[
A_i\subseteq A_j.
\]
Hence for all positive integers \(i,j\),
\[
A_i\cap A_j=A_{\gcd(i,j)}.
\]

For each positive integer \(n\), define
\[
C_n=A_n\setminus \bigcup_{d\mid n,\ d<n}A_d.
\]
Because \(A_i\cap A_j=A_{\gcd(i,j)}\), the sets \(C_n\) are pairwise disjoint, and
\[
A_n=\bigsqcup_{d\mid n} C_d.
\]
Thus
\[
n=|A_n|=\sum_{d\mid n}|C_d|.
\]
By induction and the identity
\[
n=\sum_{d\mid n}\varphi(d),
\]
we get
\[
|C_n|=\varphi(n)
\]
for every positive integer \(n\).

For a subset \(S\subseteq D\), let
\[
E(S)=\{e\in D: e\mid d \text{ for some } d\in S\}.
\]
Then \(E(S)\) is a divisor-closed subset of \(D\), and
\[
\bigcup_{d\in S}A_d=\bigsqcup_{e\in E(S)}C_e,
\]
so
\[
\left|\bigcup_{d\in S}A_d\right|=\sum_{e\in E(S)}\varphi(e).
\]

---

## 2. Minimal weights of closed divisor sets

For a divisor-closed subset \(F\subseteq D\), define its weight by
\[
W(F)=\sum_{e\in F}\varphi(e).
\]
Let \(w_k\) be the minimum possible weight of a divisor-closed subset of \(D\) having exactly \(k\) elements.

The relevant values of \(\varphi\) are

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
d&1&2&5&10&25&50&125&250\\ \hline
\varphi(d)&1&1&4&4&20&20&100&100
\end{array}
\]

Checking the divisor poset of \(250\), the minimal weights are

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
k&0&1&2&3&4&5&6&7&8\\ \hline
w_k&0&1&2&6&10&30&50&150&250
\end{array}
\]

The minimizing sets are respectively the initial segments

\[
\emptyset,\quad
\{1\},\quad
\{1,2\},\quad
\{1,2,5\},\quad
\{1,2,5,10\},
\]
\[
\{1,2,5,10,25\},\quad
\{1,2,5,10,25,50\},\quad
\{1,2,5,10,25,50,125\},\quad
D.
\]

For example, a closed set of size \(6\) either contains \(50\), forcing weight at least \(50\), or it must contain \(125\), forcing weight at least \(130\). Hence \(w_6=50\). The other values follow similarly from the divisor structure.

---

## 3. Lower bound via tail counting

For \(t\ge 0\), define
\[
N(t)=\#\{d\in D: M_d\le t\}.
\]
If \(N(t)=k\), then the union of those \(k\) sets \(A_d\) lies inside \(\{1,2,\dots,t\}\), so its size is at most \(t\). But its size is at least \(w_k\), by the previous section. Therefore
\[
w_k\le t.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
N(t)\le \max\{k:w_k\le t\}.
\]

Since
\[
\sum_{d\in D}M_d=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\#\{d\in D:M_d>t\}
=\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}(8-N(t)),
\]
we get
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}M_d
\ge
\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\left(8-\max\{k:w_k\le t\}\right).
\]

Using the values of \(w_k\), this lower bound becomes

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{d\mid 250}M_d
&\ge
(1-0)\cdot 8+(2-1)\cdot 7+(6-2)\cdot 6+(10-6)\cdot 5\\
&\qquad +(30-10)\cdot 4+(50-30)\cdot 3+(150-50)\cdot 2+(250-150)\cdot 1\\
&=8+7+24+20+80+60+200+100\\
&=499.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d\ge 499.
\]

---

## 4. Construction attaining \(499\)

We now show that \(499\) is attainable.

Choose disjoint sets \(C_n\) of positive integers such that \(|C_n|=\varphi(n)\) for all \(n\), with the following assignments for \(n\mid 250\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
C_1&=\{1\},\\
C_2&=\{2\},\\
C_5&=\{3,4,5,6\},\\
C_{10}&=\{7,8,9,10\},\\
C_{25}&=\{11,12,\dots,30\},\\
C_{50}&=\{31,32,\dots,50\},\\
C_{125}&=\{51,52,\dots,150\},\\
C_{250}&=\{151,152,\dots,250\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For all other \(n\), assign \(C_n\) any unused positive integers, still with \(|C_n|=\varphi(n)\).

Now define, for every positive integer \(m\),
\[
A_m=\bigcup_{n\mid m} C_n.
\]
Then
\[
A_i\cap A_j=\bigcup_{n\mid i,\ n\mid j}C_n
=\bigcup_{n\mid \gcd(i,j)}C_n,
\]
so
\[
|A_i\cap A_j|=\sum_{n\mid \gcd(i,j)}\varphi(n)=\gcd(i,j).
\]
Thus the required condition holds.

For \(d\mid 250\), we compute:

\[
\begin{array}{c|cccccccc}
d&1&2&5&10&25&50&125&250\\ \hline
\max A_d&1&2&6&10&30&50&150&250
\end{array}
\]

Therefore
\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d
=1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250
=499.
\]

Hence the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}.
\]
